data.body:
Frozen literals for the deleted-filename sweep (AC "No deleted filename is still referenced")

Swept all 10 deleted `_heldout.py` basenames across the whole tree with `git grep -nE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])<basename>"`, excluding `.test_durations`. Residual after the merge: **4 hits, all for one basename**, all frozen pre-fix literals recorded here per the AC's own exclusion clause.

`test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py`:
- `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/eval_specs/plan-review-T4.eval.yaml:99`
- `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/eval_specs/plan-review-T4.eval.yaml:298`
- `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/eval_specs/plan-review-T9.eval.yaml:173`
- `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/eval_specs/plan-review-T9.eval.yaml:515`

Why these are frozen and must NOT be rewritten: each is a verbatim quotation of a historical ticket's acceptance-criteria text, embedded as the recorded INPUT to a plan-review eval case ("the pre-existing `test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` continues to prove the checker's detection"). The fixture's value is that it is a byte-exact snapshot of what a reviewer was shown. Editing it to track a later rename would corrupt the recorded input and silently change what the eval measures. They are text about the past, not live path references — nothing resolves or opens them.

The other 9 basenames return **0** hits.

Provenance lines: the merge's own `# ── held-out oracles (merged from <twin>) ──` headers and `Held-out oracles merged from <twin>: …` docstring lines name the merged-away twin WITHOUT the `.py` extension, so they do not re-introduce a deleted filename. The file is gone, so naming the module rather than the file is also the more accurate form.
